title: How to Enjoy the AR Filter: Get Cuter or Funnier 😂✨
content:
Hey creators,

Are you interested in AR filters? Or do you think they've already peaked?  
If that's the case, then pay attention now! 

Create moments that are cuter and more fun than you ever imagined with AR outfits. This AR filter can be worn by anyone, from babies to adults, so experiment with your own style! 🤭💥

Try out styles you can play around with, from trendy clothes to popular meme outfits. Put on the latest fashion or surprise your friends with a laugh-inducing meme outfit! 😎👗

# **👶 Cute Version?**

We tried this AR filter on babies, and it was too cute! The little ones look absolutely adorable in their hip-hop outfits!

  


# **🤣 Funny Version?  **

But when we applied the filter to an aerobics-dressed guy? A totally different vibe! It turned into a fun vibe that had everyone laughing! 😂 You wouldn’t believe how much one filter can change the vibe!

![2944b2fbb2f44e2788ea8243d137cbdc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/03a603ec73524b37b5176dd069041e16/images/2944b2fbb2f44e2788ea8243d137cbdcapply.png)

  


# **💡 How to Use the AR Filter  **

1️⃣ Scan the QR code above. (You can use Snapchat or TikTok apps.)  
2️⃣ When the camera opens, select the filter.  
3️⃣ Try on a virtual outfit on your smartphone screen!  
4️⃣ Take a photo or video and share it on our community page or social media!

# **💡 Tips for Use!  **

✔️ Upload your photos or videos to Social Media and share them with your friends!  
✔️ Try different poses to find your unique style!  
✔️ Experiment with cute or funny versions to create different looks!

# **🎨 Want to Create Your Own?**

Would you like to create your own filter? We already have a Snapchat AR filter tutorial ready for you, [so check it out!](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/9431689555343-Tutorials)

And the best part? We're also working on a **TikTok** tutorial, so stay tuned!🎥🔥 

If you have any questions, feel free to leave a comment! 😊

  


![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/03a603ec73524b37b5176dd069041e16/images/7ab643faa62d4c03b05bef017f38e8f9thumb.png)
content_description: Discover the joy of creativity with our versatile AR filters that let everyone, from babies to adults, unleash their unique style and share fun moments!

title: Chocolate & Coffee: A Recipe with Changhun
content:
## _Discover how 3D artist Boo Changhun blends technology and creativity in Chocolate & Coffee, a virtual fashion project inspired by rich flavors and textures, crafted using CLO, Unreal Engine, and MetaHuman._

* * *

# **Interview with**  
**Boo Changhun | Lecturer & 3D Artist, CONNECT Supporters**

![2b9ec2ff57c3412d9adeb9aa1ddd2694](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/2b9ec2ff57c3412d9adeb9aa1ddd2694profile.webp)

# **How Did Changhun’s Virtual Fashion Journey Begin?**

I'm Boo Changhun, a virtual fashion lecturer and creator with five years of experience. My journey started with graphics in high school, leading to CLO in graduate school. Now, I use CLO, Twinmotion, Unreal Engine, and 3D Vista for 3D modeling.

# **What Inspired the Chocolate & Coffee Project?**

Inspired by **Mocha Mousse** , this year’s color, and my love for mocha lattes, this project captures the **balance of chocolate’s sweetness and coffee’s bitterness** in fashion design. Soft, curved elements like arched windows, ionic pillars, and ruffles reflect **chocolate’s richness** , while **coffee’s rough texture** appears in concrete, leather, and fitted silhouettes, shaping the project’s aesthetic.

![b6e0ce4dd3cc44f6818520ab19447555](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/b6e0ce4dd3cc44f6818520ab194475551.%20Mood%20Board.png)

# **How Did You Approach the Workflow for Your Chocolate & Coffee Project?**

For** _the Chocolate & Coffee project_**, I managed everything—from music to costumes, avatars, and architecture—to fully capture the desired mood. I used Metahuman for the avatar, customizing its motion and refining its face with Daz Studio's Facetransfer2, blending AI-generated images with Daz’s asset ratios for the perfect look.

![4cd5a66a170942eda83e58641b72b2f2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/4cd5a66a170942eda83e58641b72b2f22.%20Daz%20Studio%20Facetranfer2.jpg)

I imported the avatar into Unreal Engine as an FBX file, adjusting its body size, skeleton, and materials to fit Metahuman. Though tedious, this process streamlines motion creation using Unreal’s ControlRig.

![c989614905a14d22b70f00a0618af4c3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/c989614905a14d22b70f00a0618af4c33.%20Metahuman%20Identity.jpg)![67265025358e4587b3fb543059cba6a7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/67265025358e4587b3fb543059cba6a74.%20Metahuman.jpg)

I designed the clothes in CLO, blending chocolate’s softness with coffee’s rough texture through shape, color, and material. While CLO supports Metahuman avatars, I adjusted its FV2 avatar to match Metahuman’s size for rendering with AI Avatar Studio.

![82a7d65cdba7498caf1fea037af8cc3f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/82a7d65cdba7498caf1fea037af8cc3f5.%20CLO%20AI%20Avatar%20Studio%20Render.png)

Using the referenced images, CLO was used to create a central space where chocolate flows into Mocha Mousse color, with one side featuring rough concrete and the other showcasing an arch-shaped window and Ionic column.

![652af7f425684185bb4f4acb1156ec87](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/652af7f425684185bb4f4acb1156ec876.%20Building%20Modeling.jpg)![d1d73c819b3b44d48267311c7142f8c2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/d1d73c819b3b44d48267311c7142f8c27.%20Building%20modeling%202.png)

To visually convey the concept, CLO created objects like chocolate-filled columns, mugs, coffee beans, and leather sofas. These objects, along with the designed spaces, were exported to Unreal Engine in OBJ format and scaled accordingly.

![45fc48d98d8b498d8206ca7999ddac58](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/45fc48d98d8b498d8206ca7999ddac588.%20Object%20Modeling.jpg)

Materials were created using Unreal Engine’s Blueprint function, with concrete textures from Quixel Bridge, and chocolate and coffee textures generated using Photoshop’s AI tool, alongside other materials for smooth chocolate effects.

![94c2d5a4a32141bc94b564fb69b8a743](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/94c2d5a4a32141bc94b564fb69b8a7439.%20Chocolate%20%26%20Coffee%20Material.png)![9669fef361864a7294f1e459e88af347](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/9669fef361864a7294f1e459e88af34710.%20Space%20Material.png)

The body and facial expressions of the Metahuman avatar were recorded frame by frame using ControlRig and saved as an animation.

![fb162395012040b9910135ea1c41e53f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/fb162395012040b9910135ea1c41e53f11.%20Controlrig.jpg)

The recorded animations of the faces and bodies were exported as FBX files and imported into CLO, where they were then applied to the clothing animations.

![5ffc242d1d9e4b6abd44df1e00b6cc4a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/5ffc242d1d9e4b6abd44df1e00b6cc4a12.%20Animation%20Recording.jpg)

After recording the animation, the costume animation was imported into Unreal Engine using the LiveSync feature. The geometry cache of the costume was saved to align the avatar's position, simplifying the rendering of the animation with the costume matching the avatar's movement.

![4c0b608a57aa46cea60e4e7f205016e3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/4c0b608a57aa46cea60e4e7f205016e313.%20Metahuman%20in%20Clothing.jpg)

# **What Challenges Did You Face, and How Did You Overcome Them?**

A major challenge was mesh distortion and crashes when importing CLO garments into Unreal Engine via LiveSync, often due to stretched or tangled patterns near the avatar’s arms. To fix this, I adjusted Metahuman’s control rig motion to keep body parts apart. For close-contact movements, I rendered the final animation using a costume without a collision pattern, preventing mesh errors.

![43a34636d8f24e58bdd61ef30ba32c21](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/43a34636d8f24e58bdd61ef30ba32c2114.%20Pose%20with%20Open%20Arms.png)![a74fde8e21734b52a735bf32bd2dc2c5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d96edbf27767493daca714ae0bf750eb/images/a74fde8e21734b52a735bf32bd2dc2c515.%20Sleeveless%20Clothing.png)

* * *

# **How has CONNECT and CLO helped in your design process?**

**_The Chocolate & Coffee Project _**modified CONNECT's block patterns, streamlining early-stage design and enabling broader exploration. CLO, initially fashion-focused, proved versatile for modeling beyond fabric, sparking my interest in using it for solid structures like buildings. With intuitive tools like LiveSync, CLO empowers fashion designers to explore broader 3D modeling, unlocking endless creative possibilities.

* * *

Explore Changhun's portfolio and follow his creative journey on social media!

  * [_CONNECT Portfolio_](https://connect.clo-set.com/portfolio/108694/collection/collections)

  *  _Instagram_[ _@fadyboo_](https://www.instagram.com/fadyboo/)
content_description: Explore how 3D artist Boo Changhun seamlessly fuses technology and creativity in his Chocolate & Coffee virtual fashion project, inspired by the rich flavors and textures of mocha lattes.

title: [Contest Reminder📢] D-12 Until the Deadline! FAQ Summary✨
content:
# **_📢Contest Reminder📢_**

![5298a4dc0f3f40d1ad720e1cde09f5e5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/1347019934474c8785d1aa5da492fa23/images/5298a4dc0f3f40d1ad720e1cde09f5e5CONNECT_News%20Letter.png)

Hey everyone!   
⏳ The contest deadline is approaching!   
Are you all set?   
If you haven't started yet, no worries! It's never too late to join.🔥

💰 **A $5,700 prize is waiting for the winner!**   
Don't miss your chance to showcase your talent and take home the reward!

* * *

**📌 Quick Contest Overview**

  * 👗 Theme: Choose your favorite K-Pop stars and recreate their outfits with precision.

  * 📅 Deadline: April 07, 2025

  * 🎨 Submission Method: Submit on the contest page **(Don't forget to include your reference image!)**

  * ❓ Want to know more? Just follow this [**[LINK]**](https://connect.clo-set.com/contest/k-popmirror)**!**




* * *

_Also! We've compiled_** _the most frequently asked questions_** _._  
_👇👇👇Make sure to check them before submitting!👇👇👇_

# **❓ Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)**

**Q1. Can I recreate outfits from K-dramas or K-virtual idols instead of K-pop?  
** 👉 Yes, you can! As long as your design is inspired by the K-pop genre, outfits from K-dramas or K-virtual idols are also allowed.

**Q2. Is this a worldwide contest?  
** 👉 Yes! Participants from all over the world can join. However, please note that prize distribution may not be available in certain countries. Check the [**Contest Reward part**](https://connect.clo-set.com/contest/k-popmirror) for more details.

**Q3. Can I use other software?  
** 👉 Yes! As stated in the guidelines, you're free to use other tools for background design and rendering. However, **you must use CLO3D or Marvelous Designer for outfit creation.**

**Q4. Do I need to match every detail of the reference image? Can the pose be different?  
** 👉 While it's ideal to match the pose, **the main judging criteria focus on how accurately the outfit is recreated.** Poses can enhance the overall presentation, but the key evaluation points are **the outfit’s accuracy and execution.**

* * *

# 📢 **Got more questions?, visit**[**[HERE]**](https://connect.clo-set.com/contest/k-popmirror)**!**

Feel free to ask in the comments, on the Q&A board, or through our [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/closet_connect_official/).  
We can't wait to see your amazing creations! Keep going and give it your best shot!🔥💖

**With passion** 🔥**,**  
**The CONNECT Team**

title: GATHERING
content:
![e1a2b25e0fa942fd87ab3ee5a14c749a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d6dea7f97a8043d6b869f04d3b3a64a1/images/e1a2b25e0fa942fd87ab3ee5a14c749agather%20.png)![dcf60d7427904ce890285ddff323ad32](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/d6dea7f97a8043d6b869f04d3b3a64a1/images/dcf60d7427904ce890285ddff323ad32gather%20back%20.png)

Hi CLO community i'm trying to gather on the skirt part of this dress, ive tried many ways to gather put just can nit get it to look good or neat or realistic can any help out and advise me. Thanks :)

* * *


### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I’ve done this feature before. I added a thin strip 1cm wide behind the side seam. I then made the strip half the length of the seam which made it all gather up. Make sure your particle distance number is low. Number 3 if your computer can handle it. This will help get a realistic effect.
Reply 1: Thank you for this, every time I change the particle distance the arrow is just spinning round, I've put this on 3 , my computer is more that what I need for the CLO software. Have you got any other advise about this. I have now change it back to 1.00 and it simulates. I will now try making the strips 1cm wide and see if this works.

Comment 2: Hi, the look and realism of fine details like this are heavily affected by the Particle Distance, Add'l Thickness Collision, etc. Another, or additional, option to use would be shirring on the side seams so that you can get a better idea of the outcome without compromising the speed of your simulation as you are working on the garment.https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/d6dea7f97a8043d6b869f04d3b3a64a1

title: How Hilary Brought Taylor Swift's Eras Tour Gown to Life in CLO
content:
## _Hilary Martin, a talented patternmaker, is exploring the world of 3D design with CLO._

## _Using CLO, Hilary quickly transformed her design ideas, showcasing the power of digital fashion. Discover her process behind recreating this unforgettable gown._

* * *

![1f2393fdf7e14a01b9a7239f9d5fc184](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/ec79cb82573d499ab9c46e4184a635ba/images/1f2393fdf7e14a01b9a7239f9d5fc184Userspotlight_1080w.png)

### **Can you introduce yourself and share a bit about your background?**

I’ve been sewing my own clothes since childhood and studied fashion design in New Zealand. I gravitated toward patternmaking at university because it blends logic and creativity. I took every patternmaking class I could during my degree. Eleven years ago, I moved to Melbourne, Australia, to pursue a career in design and have since worked across accessories, apparel, and denim.  
Currently, I design bags and accessories for an Australian label. For me, great design is all about function and practicality so designing bags is a great place to flex those skills. While I don’t use CLO at work yet, I felt it was important to upskill as 3D is slowly working its way into the Australian fashion industry. I’ve been teaching myself for about a year.

### **Your background in patternmaking is really interesting! How has that experience shaped the way you approach 3D design?**

### I’m more excited about using CLO for pattern making than for creating hyper-realistic renders of finished garments. I spent the weekend experimenting with a dress design—changing the pattern again and again and seeing the results in real time. It allowed me to come up with something unique and innovative incredibly quickly. The same process with manual pattern making and physical sampling would have taken me weeks.

![5a7def4441c84d6f81bfc78c906687a2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/ec79cb82573d499ab9c46e4184a635ba/images/5a7def4441c84d6f81bfc78c906687a2Screenshot%202025-03-04%20210738.png)![fabb6c5b31cd4bf2b4633f64dbc88c36](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/ec79cb82573d499ab9c46e4184a635ba/images/fabb6c5b31cd4bf2b4633f64dbc88c36Screenshot%202025-03-04%20210828.png)

### **Could you share the story or inspiration behind this recreation of Taylor Swift’s gown on the Eras Tour? Have you recreated any other pieces in the past?**

### I learn best by doing, so I’ve been teaching myself CLO through a variety of projects. Each one has helped me master different tools and skills within the program. When I saw Taylor Swift wearing her incredible Vivienne Westwood gown on the Eras Tour, I thought it would be a fun challenge to recreate! This dress was only the third garment I had created in CLO, so it required a lot of trial and error—as well as plenty of YouTube tutorials. Now that I’m more confident, I’m focusing on my own original designs. I love tailoring, so I’m currently working on a winter coat.

### **Can you expand on how CLO has influenced your overall approach to design beyond just patternmaking?**

### CLO has definitely made me a more experimental designer. It’s completely changed the way I approach the design process because I’m no longer limited by the time, cost, or materials needed for physical sampling. I can quickly cycle through different ideas—tweaking a pattern, swapping fabrics, testing colorways—without any of the usual constraints. It’s also made me more willing to take risks. Before CLO, I might have second-guessed whether a complex design was worth the time and resources to sample. Now, I can push an idea further, knowing that I can work through construction challenges digitally first. It’s taken so much of the guesswork out of the process, and I find myself exploring ideas I wouldn’t have attempted before.

![00c0e4000d874f26b1a43c9ea2bc1593](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/ec79cb82573d499ab9c46e4184a635ba/images/00c0e4000d874f26b1a43c9ea2bc1593combined%20%281%29.png)

### **Since you have such a strong hands-on design background, what was it like transitioning to 3D with CLO? Were there any surprises along the way?**

### Learning CLO felt mostly intuitive, especially since some functions—like bezier curves and curve points—are similar to Illustrator, which I'm very fluent in. The biggest learning curve was navigating the 3D window (using the gizmo, etc.) and learning where all the tools were. Initially, I was skeptical about how well the software could handle complex draping, so I digitized one of my more unconventional patterns—it has large bias-cut panels, curves sewn onto curves, seams that twist around the body in unusual ways, gathers, and a button-up placket - and CLO replicated the garment in 3D form perfectly.

### **Is there a moment where CLO really saved the day for you—maybe solving a tricky design challenge that would’ve been much harder using traditional methods?**

### Another thing I’ve found really useful in CLO is the ability to visualize print placement before cutting. I recently made a bias-cut dress with a strong directional stripe print and was able to move the print around within the pattern pieces, ensuring that the stripes all converged perfectly at a central seam beneath the bust. Being able to visualize many different print placements before deciding on the final design is a big advantage over traditional methods.

### **When you start a new project, what’s your creative process like? Do you follow a set routine, or is it more spontaneous?**

### In my professional work, everything follows a structured process. The creative director sets the color palette and mood, and we work within a strict critical path. In my personal projects, however, I tend to have multiple ideas running simultaneously. Some projects come together in a day, while others take months. I find that the most interesting ideas emerge when I allow myself to get into a creative flow state and simply follow the process.

![594aab4e7bb049f1a955495f64aeec40](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/ec79cb82573d499ab9c46e4184a635ba/images/594aab4e7bb049f1a955495f64aeec40combined%20%282%29.png)

### **Looking back at this project, what part of the process was the most fun or rewarding for you?**  
Eveningwear isn’t my specialty, so this project was a real experiment for me. Before CLO, I probably wouldn’t have attempted something like this—I would have stuck to what I knew. But 3D design allows you to make mistakes and correct them quickly without wasting materials or time. That’s an incredible advantage, and I wish I had started learning it sooner!

### **Was there a specific CLO tool or feature that really stood out for you while working on this piece?  
** I used the 3D Pen Avatar for the bodice, and it was surprisingly easy—the fit was perfect on the first go. Since it works a lot like the pen tool in Illustrator, I got the hang of it quickly. The skirt was a whole different challenge—getting the pleats and tucks to fold and drape properly with the Fold tool took quite a few tries!

![00b413f3a16a40458197b8fc1d2595a9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202503/ec79cb82573d499ab9c46e4184a635ba/images/00b413f3a16a40458197b8fc1d2595a9LINEN%20DRESS.png)

  
**You mentioned focusing on original designs now—what’s your design philosophy when it comes to creating your own pieces? How do you decide which materials and styles to work with?  
** I like to make sure every piece has a point of difference. Lately, I’ve been creating a lot of one-off pieces and trying to unlearn some of the rules we’re taught when designing for mass production. For example, I had a piece of wool with text along the selvedge that I thought was really beautiful, so I incorporated the selvedge into the garment. In mass production, placing a pattern piece strictly along the selvedge wouldn’t be an economical use of fabric, so it wouldn’t typically be done. Sometimes, I fall in love with a piece of fabric first and try to create something that highlights its unique drape or texture. Other times, I’m focused on achieving a particular silhouette, so the design ends up being very pattern-led. And sometimes, I’m inspired by another garment and try to replicate it with a point of difference. My favorite fabric is wool—I love how it can be sculpted with sewing, heat, and steam.

**What advice would you give to aspiring digital fashion designers who want to follow in your footsteps?  
** Start now, but be patient with the learning process. I’m only just reaching the point where I can design fluidly in CLO without constantly stopping to search for tools or rewatch tutorials. Once everything clicks, the creative possibilities are incredible. I haven’t felt this excited about learning something new since I was first taught how to patternmake nearly 18 years ago.
content_description: Explore Hilary Martin's journey as a patternmaker transitioning to 3D design with CLO, where she showcases her innovative process and creative experimentation in digital fashion.
